newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta Fed economist says factory prices subdued.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta Fed economist says factory prices subdued.

text.p: Despite another jump in the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank survey's prices paid index, manufacturing prices remain "subdued" in the southeastern United States, said Mark Rogers, an economist at the Atlanta Fed.

"Prices paid is not near where it was in portions of 1994 and 1995," Rogers said in an interview with Reuters. "So, I do not interpret the latest price numbers as an indication of inflationary pressures."
He added that the index has come up from very low levels seen a few months ago.
The prices paid index rose to 18.1 in February, from 17.2 in January, while the prices received index edged up to 1.0 from -2.5.
The overall Atlanta Fed index fell to 7.0 from a revised 13.8, but the fact that the index remained above zero suggested a healthy maufacturing picture, Rogers said.
Still, he noted that the Southeastern region was growing at a "less robust" pace than that of the overall U.S.
"All indications are that momentum of manufacturing in the Southeast is at a moderate pace ... along with real subdued manufacturing prices," he said.
As for the decline in the employment index in February to -0.6 from 2.5, Rogers said the trend remained steady, with few layoffs and new hires.
He noted that after a volatile few months of numbers, the overall diffusion index appears to be moderating.

Meanwhile, Rogers said it was clear from the 0.8 percent rise in February retail sales that consumer spending continues to do better. "The mix nationally is that demand is picking up, but I am not sure if it will carry over into price increases," Rogers said.

"It is safe to say the structure of the economy has changed substantially over the years," he added. "The economy is less inflation prone, yet it can accelerate with strong (consumer) demand and tight labor markets. The question is to what extent the structure has changed."
